record.context_brief: Ambrose problem for exponential pullback metrics
record.original_question: Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, let p be a point of M, and let h be the pullback of g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM -> M, allowing h to degenerate where exp_p fails to be regular. Does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M, g, p) uniquely up to isometry?

evidence.quote: Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, and let p ∈ M. Denote by h the pullback of the metric tensor g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM → M; in general, h might degenerate at some points. Does h define the manifold (M, g) and the point p up to isometry?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a simply connected, complete Riemannian manifold and let $p\in M$. Consider the exponential map $\exp_p\colon T_pM\to M$ based at $p$, and define the symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor
$$h := \exp_p^{*} g$$
on the tangent space $T_pM$ (regarded as a smooth manifold diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{\dim M}$). At points where $\exp_p$ fails to be a local diffeomorphism, $h$ is allowed to be degenerate.

Question: Does the (possibly degenerate) tensor $h$ on $T_pM$ determine the pointed Riemannian manifold $(M,g,p)$ uniquely up to pointed isometry? That is, if $(M_1,g_1,p_1)$ and $(M_2,g_2,p_2)$ are two such simply connected complete pointed Riemannian manifolds and there exists a linear isometry $L\colon T_{p_1}M_1\to T_{p_2}M_2$ with $L^{*}(\exp_{p_2}^{*}g_2)=\exp_{p_1}^{*}g_1$, must there exist an isometry $\Phi\colon (M_1,g_1)\to(M_2,g_2)$ with $\Phi(p_1)=p_2$ and $d\Phi_{p_1}=L$?
artifact.status_search_result: The classical Ambrose problem—whether a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold is determined by parallel-translated curvature data along geodesics from a point—is known to be solved in dimension 2 (Hebda, Itoh) but remains open in higher dimensions. The specific reformulation using the degenerate pullback tensor $\exp_p^*g$ on $T_pM$ does not appear to have a published resolution; no source verifying its solution was located.

status_evidence.title: Cartan–Ambrose–Hicks theorem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the Cartan–Ambrose–Hicks theorem and the still-unresolved Ambrose conjecture in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The Ambrose problem on global determination of a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold from data at a point remains open in general.
